To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the integration of emotion expression and locomotive behaviors makes the humanoid robot perceived by humans as more appealing and more human like.
the integration of dynamic emotions and locomotion makes a humanoid robot more appealing and more useful for human robot interaction.
the dynamical expression of the emotions in a humanoid robot, based on a mental model, is perceived as more favorable, useful, and less robot like, compared to the static emotion expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a dynamic mental model in a humanoid robot to improve human robot interaction and to make the robot more human-like.
the implementation of the mental model of emotions in a humanoid robot, and the evaluation of the importance of this model for the interaction between the robot and humans.
the design and development of a humanoid robot capable of expressing emotions in a natural and effective way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed system is able to generate a more "human-like" behavior, which in turn increases the perceived "human-likeness" of the robot, and makes it more "appealing" to humans.
the proposed system allows to increase the social acceptation of the humanoid robot, and to improve its perceived social skills.

the integration of the dynamical emotion expression with locomotion makes the robot more appealing to the human, as it is percieved as more "useful" (and less "robot like"), and that it is perceived as a more "favorable robot" to be used in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have implemented a mental model in a humanoid robot to dynamically change its emotional state based on external stimuli, and that the integration of emotion expression and locomotions makes the humanoid robot perceived as more "human like" and "favorable" by humans.

we have implemented a mental model in a whole body humanoid robot, and the dynamical change in the emotional state of this robot is perceived by humans as more natural than a robot that does not change its emotions.
the integration of the dynamic emotion expression and locomotin makes the humanoid robot much more appealing to humans as it is perceived to be more favorable and useful and less robot-like.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamical change and the whole body expression of the emotions in the robot make it more attractive and more useful for human robot interaction.
the integration of a dynamic emotional system in a humanoid robot can improve human robot interaction.
a humanoid robot with a dynamical emotional state is more appealing to people than a humanoid without emotions.
